items.bold: IRAN PROPOSED: Reopen Hormuz + end war — DEFER nuclear to later. Staged two-track proposal.
items.text: AP (Monday, two regional officials): Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war in exchange for US lifting its naval blockade, while deferring nuclear talks to a later phase. Reuters (senior Iranian officials): staged approach — first end war with no-restart guarantees, then resolve blockade + Hormuz, nuclear later. Most concrete formal proposal since February 28. Nuclear decoupling is deliberate — Iran sees Hormuz as a ceasefire/sovereignty issue, nuclear as a separate long-term negotiation. Trump told reporters Saturday Iran sent a "much better" proposal. WH confirmed NSC reviewed it Monday.

items.bold: TRUMP NOT SATISFIED — nuclear not addressed. WSJ: White House counterproposal coming in days.
items.text: NYT (briefed on Monday NSC meeting): Trump told advisers he is not satisfied — nuclear programme not addressed. Reuters: Trump wants nuclear at the start, not deferred. WSJ: Trump did NOT reject outright — White House will likely make a counterproposal in coming days. WH: "will not negotiate through press, clear about red lines." Rubio (Fox News): "fundamental issue of nuclear must still be confronted — can't let them buy time." CNN: unlikely to accept as-is — lifting blockade without nuclear resolution weakens US leverage. Vance (The Atlantic): privately worried war is depleting US weapons stockpiles and Pentagon giving Trump overly rosy picture.

items.bold: ARAGHCHI MET PUTIN in St Petersburg — 1.5hr. Putin confirmed Mojtaba Khamenei message.
items.text: NPR (updated April 27) and AFP photo confirmed: Araghchi met Putin at Boris Yeltsin Presidential Library, St Petersburg. 1.5hr meeting. Putin confirmed receiving message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — who has not been seen publicly since becoming Supreme Leader. Araghchi: meeting "very good," "very good ideas put forward," "very good grounds for continued cooperation." Kremlin: "importance of this conversation is difficult to overestimate." Russia confirmed as deal guarantor.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 9:30 PM IST. Day 60 of the West Asia War. Two days of the most significant diplomatic movement since February 28 — with no deal yet.

THE IRAN PROPOSAL
• Iran: reopen Hormuz + end war in exchange for US lifting blockade
• Nuclear talks: deferred to a later phase
• Staged approach: (1) end war; (2) resolve blockade + Hormuz; (3) nuclear later
• Delivered via Pakistan to US
• Most concrete formal proposal since February 28

THE US RESPONSE — NOT SATISFIED, BUT NOT REJECTED
• Trump: not satisfied — nuclear not addressed (NYT)
• Trump: Iran sent "much better" proposal (Saturday, before formal NSC review)
• WSJ: White House will likely make a counterproposal in coming days
• Rubio: proposal unacceptable — nuclear must be confronted first
• CNN: unlikely to accept as-is — lifting blockade without nuclear weakens leverage
• Vance: privately worried war is depleting US weapons stockpiles

THE RUSSIA FACTOR
• Araghchi met Putin in St Petersburg — 1.5 hours
• Also met Lavrov + Russia military intelligence chief
• Putin confirmed he received a message from Mojtaba Khamenei
• Putin: "Will do everything to help secure peace"
• Russia confirmed as deal guarantor — critical for Iran's security guarantee requirement

THE OIL SHOCK DEEPENING
• Brent $111.49 — 7th consecutive session gain
• UAE leaving OPEC Friday (partial offset)
• US clearing mines in Hormuz
• Iran using rail delivery + Caspian + junk storage for crude
• Even a deal today: 4-6 months to normalise
• India OMC hike Rs 4-8/L — IMMINENT

INDIA AT DAY 60
• 60 days of war. Crude buffer EXHAUSTED
• Sensex 76,887. Nifty 23,996 (below 24k)
• OMC petrol/diesel hike Rs 4-8/L — most significant consumer price shock of the war
• Kharif fertiliser: at risk if Hormuz closed through May
• Coal India, Nifty Metal, Oil & Gas — only sectors working
• WH counterproposal in days = next market catalyst

40-35-25 CALL
• 40%: WH counterproposal bridges gap → Brent $90-95, Nifty 24,200-24,500
• 35%: Stalemate, proposals and counterproposals → Brent $110-115, Nifty 23,500-24,000
• 25%: Nuclear standoff → breakdown, resumed strikes → Brent $130+, Nifty 60,000

VERDICT: Day 60 ends with the West Asia War in its most diplomatically active and most economically destructive phase simultaneously. Iran made a real proposal. Trump rejected the nuclear decoupling. A counterproposal is coming. Brent is at $111. India's crude buffer is exhausted. The White House counterproposal in the coming days will determine whether this war ends in a deal or escalates into its most dangerous chapter yet.
